title: Exponential of a Kronecker sum factors as a Kronecker product of exponentials
expression_sketch:
Let A lie in C^{m x m} and B in C^{n x n}. Write I_k for the k x k identity and define the Kronecker sum A oplus B := A tensor I_n + I_m tensor B. Then
  exp(A tensor I_n + I_m tensor B) = exp(A) tensor exp(B).
Sibling trigonometric identities on the same generator (Higham Theorem 12.2):
  sin(A oplus B) = sin(A) tensor cos(B) + cos(A) tensor sin(B),
  cos(A oplus B) = cos(A) tensor cos(B) - sin(A) tensor sin(B).
The factorisation uses that A tensor I_n and I_m tensor B commute, so the exponential of their sum is the product of exponentials, which then mixed-multiplies to exp(A) tensor exp(B). No spectral restriction: exp is entire.
latent_structure: One MATRIX_FUNCTION master, the exponential (or sine/cosine) of a Kronecker sum, factors as a tensor product of the same function on the summands. The commuting pair (A tensor I, I tensor B) is the generator; mixed-product reconstruction recovers the tensor identity. The trigonometric pair is the same master applied to the even/odd parts of exp(iZ).

function_domains.exp: Entire on C; primary matrix exponential defined for every square complex matrix by the power series (Higham Chapter 10, definition of e^A).
function_domains.sin: Entire on C; primary matrix sine (Higham Chapter 12).
function_domains.cos: Entire on C; primary matrix cosine (Higham Chapter 12).

analytic_domains.statement: The identity exp(A tensor I_n + I_m tensor B) = exp(A) tensor exp(B) holds for all A in C^{m x m} and all B in C^{n x n}; exp is entire so there is no spectral restriction (Higham Theorem 10.9).
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Higham, Functions of Matrices, SIAM 2008, Theorem 10.9

analytic_domains.statement: The identities sin(A oplus B) = sin(A) tensor cos(B) + cos(A) tensor sin(B) and cos(A oplus B) = cos(A) tensor cos(B) - sin(A) tensor sin(B) hold for all square complex A, B of compatible size (Higham Theorem 12.2).
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Higham, Functions of Matrices, SIAM 2008, Theorem 12.2

branch_conventions: Primary matrix exponential, sine, and cosine via power series; not entrywise transcendental functions.
Kronecker product is the standard block embedding (A tensor B)_{ij} = a_{ij} B; Kronecker sum is A tensor I_n + I_m tensor B, not the direct sum diag(A,B).
source_provenance: N. J. Higham, Functions of Matrices: Theory and Computation, SIAM, 2008, Theorem 10.9 and Theorem 12.2. DOI 10.1137/1.9780898717778
M. Benzi, V. Simoncini, Approximation of functions of large matrices with Kronecker structure, Numer. Math. 135 (2017) 1-26, arXiv:1503.02615, equation (6) citing Higham Theorem 10.9
R. A. Horn, C. R. Johnson, Topics in Matrix Analysis, Cambridge University Press, 1991/1994, p. 208 (Kronecker-sum exponential)

derived_conditions.statement: A tensor I_n and I_m tensor B commute, because (A tensor I_n)(I_m tensor B) = A tensor B = (I_m tensor B)(A tensor I_n). Hence exp(X+Y)=exp(X)exp(Y) applies to X = A tensor I_n and Y = I_m tensor B (Higham Theorem 10.2 / handbook Fact 1 of the exponential section).
derived_conditions.label: DERIVED
derived_conditions.source: Higham, Functions of Matrices, SIAM 2008, Theorem 10.9 (standard proof via commuting exponentials); Higham handbook chapter, exponential Fact 1

public_source: N. J. Higham, Functions of Matrices, SIAM 2008, Theorem 10.9 and Theorem 12.2, DOI 10.1137/1.9780898717778. Restatement: Benzi--Simoncini, arXiv:1503.02615, eq. (6). Horn--Johnson, Topics in Matrix Analysis, p. 208.
why_not_cse_lgg: The left-hand side is the exponential of an mn x mn sum of Kronecker embeddings; the right-hand side is a tensor of two smaller exponentials. CSE will not factor that sum through the mixed-product identity. LGG will not invent Kronecker sum as a generator whose exponential is a tensor product, nor produce the sine/cosine addition formulae on the same generator.
proposer_leak_risk: Hide Kronecker sum, mixed-product, commuting embeddings. Catalog members are the expanded operators A tensor I + I tensor B, exp(A) tensor exp(B), and the two trigonometric expansions.
notes: Do not insert self-adjointness, stability, or a Lyapunov/Sylvester equation; the identity is an equality of matrix functions, not a linear matrix equation. Do not confuse Kronecker sum with the direct sum diag(A,B). Do not insert a spectral gap. Theorem 10.9 is unrestricted because exp is entire.
